judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line definition; 'becomes uncontrollable or breaks out from where it was intended to be' is settled insurance language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in the two hostile-fire exceptions to the pollution exclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition uses lettered limbs a. and b. twice in one sentence for different purposes, which makes the restoration test awkward to read; 'known or thought to be defective' is also loose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Feeds exclusion m. and the recall exclusion, both of which are drafted around it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb f. is a broad residual ('that part of any other contract or agreement pertaining to your business') sitting after five specific categories, with three further carve-outs — the classic general-versus-specific structure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is engaged by the Contractual Liability exclusion and by the Supplementary Payments indemnitee provision, and its lease carve-out for fire damage coordinates with the Damage To Premises Rented To You limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short definition with an express exclusion of temporary workers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates precisely with Definitions 5 and 19 and with Who Is An Insured.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three lettered stages plus a mechanical-device carve-out; precise, though 'hand truck' is an oddly specific line to draw.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in the aircraft/auto/watercraft exclusion and in Definition 16.b.(1); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Other vehicles designed for use principally off public roads' is a general catch-all after specific examples, and the closing deeming rule converts some listed items into 'autos' — a structure that repays argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interlocks with the 'auto' definition and with the aircraft/auto/watercraft and mobile equipment exclusions, which cross-refer to its lettered limbs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Accident' is left undefined and is one of the most heavily litigated words in liability insurance, though the continuous-exposure rider is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives the Each Occurrence Limit and the Coverage A trigger, both of which assume the term is workable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of seven offenses; limb c. (wrongful eviction, wrongful entry, invasion of the right of private occupancy) is a well-known battleground for a landlord risk.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: For an apartment owner, limb c. sits against exclusion j.(1) and the Employment-Related Practices endorsement, so its scope has to be worked out across provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The same broad-plus-illustrative 'irritant or contaminant' definition that regularly draws ejusdem generis argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to the property-form definitions, so at least the instrument is internally consistent on the term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but tightly structured, with three deeming rules for when work is complete and three express exclusions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph b.(3) removes from the hazard any operation whose classification says products-completed operations are subject to the General Aggregate — which is exactly what the classification schedule says here — so the separate Products-Completed Operations Aggregate in the Declarations may be left with nothing to cover.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reproduction badly corrupts the electronic-data sentence, and the two limbs plus their deemed-timing rules are conceptually dense even when clean.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'loss of use' limb interacts with exclusion m. and the impaired property definition, and the electronic data carve-out parallels the property forms' treatment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition with two enumerated inclusions; the consent requirement for ADR proceedings is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Drives the duty to defend in Coverages A and B and the Supplementary Payments provision; consistent throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short definition; 'seasonal or short-term workload conditions' is mildly open but concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with Definitions 5 and 10 to produce a coherent worker taxonomy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three cumulative requirements; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in Who Is An Insured and in the Coverage C 'any insured' exclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The numbering is corrupted (item 5 appears as 'a' and item 6 as '&'), yet items 5 and 6 expressly cross-refer to 'parts 1. through 4.' and 'parts 1. through 5.', so the internal references do not match the printed labels.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps the pollution exclusion without saying which controls, and it is a manuscript State Auto form sitting beside the ISO exclusions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two printed columns are merged, so the Coverage A exclusion is interleaved with the Coverage B exclusion and the limbs appear twice in scrambled order.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The merged Coverage B material is separately reproduced at c282, so the same exclusion appears twice in the instrument in overlapping fragments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same column merge, with the 'This exclusion applies' block appearing twice and the bodily-injury and personal-injury limbs interleaved.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c281; the two provisions cannot be told apart on their face.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reproduction is severely corrupted — the Coverage B limb reads 'Personai would nob place, in whole or in actual, alleged or threat...' — so large parts of the exclusion are unreadable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same corrupted Coverage B text is reproduced again at c284, and this fungi exclusion overlaps the property form's Limited Coverage For 'Fungus' in a different coverage part.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same corruption: the operative exclusion sentence is fragmentary and the abatement limb appears twice in different states.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c283, so the instrument carries two overlapping renderings of a single exclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A circular but conventionally enumerated definition of 'fungi'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the 'fungus' definitions in CP 00 10 and CP 10 30 in substance, though the property forms use the singular spelling and this one uses 'fungi'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The lead-in 'added to all coverages contained within' is loose, and limb 1 excludes only 'bodily injury' from ingestion, inhalation or absorption while limb 2 excludes property and advertising injury 'arising out of any form of lead' — a deliberate asymmetry that is easy to argue about.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps the pollution exclusion without a priority rule, and it names a Businessowners Liability Coverage Form that is not part of this policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional exclusion with three enumerated triggers, all resting on defined terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: IL 09 60 already contains an equivalent exclusion for the property part with only two triggers (it omits the nuclear limb), so the policy carries two differently scoped terrorism exclusions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Includes but is not limited to' followed by a list of defined injury types is an open-ended catch-all after specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to 'injury' and 'environmental damage' as defined in 'any applicable Coverage Part', but no coverage part in this policy defines those terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory definition with a clean two-part criterion; precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The duplicate printing of this same endorsement at c299 states the threshold as '$45 million' rather than $5 million, so the policy contains two inconsistent versions of the same definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening line is corrupted, and the substantive test ('appears to be part of an effort to coerce a civilian population') is evaluative, though the 72-hour aggregation rule is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The corresponding IL 09 60 property definition omits the 72-hour aggregation rule, so the two terrorism regimes in the policy differ.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short savings clause; as reproduced a stray 'D' interrupts the sentence but the meaning survives.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to IL 09 60 D for the property part; consistent in function.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'However caused, arising, directly or indirectly, out of' is deliberately sweeping, but the three limbs are enumerated and closed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly replaces exclusion i. reproduced at c203, which is far narrower (confined to contractually assumed liability), so the printed form and the endorsement state materially different exclusions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mirrors the Coverage A war exclusion with the same three limbs; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coverage B previously had no war exclusion, so this is a pure addition rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A slightly convoluted sentence that disapplies exclusion h. and reroutes war medical payments through exclusion g.; the reasoning is stated but the double negative takes work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly displaces the Coverage C war exclusion reproduced at c234, which remains printed in the form, so the two must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short exclusion of punitive damages tied to a defined term; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is duplicated word for word at c303, and its definition of 'certified act of terrorism' must match the versions in the other terrorism endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory definition with a clean two-part criterion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c289 and c304 at $5 million, but inconsistent with the '$45 million' figure printed at c299.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As reproduced the exclusion has the endorsement's own title block and schedule of coverage parts spliced into the middle of its operative sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a verbatim duplicate of the endorsement at c287, so the same terrorism exclusion is attached twice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Includes but is not limited to' after a specific list is an open catch-all, as in the first printing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A verbatim duplicate of c288, and it again refers to 'injury' and 'environmental damage' as defined terms that no coverage part in this policy defines.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It states the certification threshold as 'aggregate losses in excess of $45 million', which is a plain mechanical error against the federal Act and against every other printing of the same definition in this policy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c289, c296 and c304 all state $5 million for the identical definition, so the instrument contains two irreconcilable thresholds for the same defined term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening is corrupted but the substance survives; the coercion test is evaluative and the 72-hour aggregation rule is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A duplicate of c290, and it uses the $5 million carve-out that sits against the '$45 million' figure in the same duplicated endorsement at c299.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short savings clause; clean in this printing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A verbatim duplicate of c291.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short statutory cap; its content is fixed by the federal Act rather than by ambiguous policy words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates the cap provisions at c184 and in the first CG 21 72 printing, so the same limitation appears several times across the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence punitive damages exclusion; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A verbatim duplicate of c295, so the same endorsement is attached twice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory definition with a clean two-part criterion; the '$5 million' figure is correct.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates c296 and contradicts the '$45 million' figure in the duplicate CG 21 72 endorsement at c299.
